label: Ringside flash
prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: revision of the supplied boxing-game concept frame. Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Make exactly these two environmental changes: (1) remove ALL lettering, words and slogans from the walls, wall posters, spectator placards/signboards and other in-world scenery, including corner pads, ring mat and bucket if present. Keep the existing worn brick, paper, paint, plastic and lighting: posters and remaining placards can be plain worn coloured shapes, with no words, no fake glyphs and no replacement slogans. (2) reduce the visible spectator population to approximately HALF of the input image's count, retaining roughly every other spectator and spacing the survivors naturally. Show clear gaps between spectators; do not hide a full crowd in a new rear row or replace removed people with silhouettes. Keep both central fighters unchanged. Everything else must remain the same: camera, composition, fighter identities, articulated toy construction, poses, gloves, ring ropes, arena dimensions, dramatic lighting, colour palette, health bars and complete bottom control rail with exactly three knobs, ATTACK/STANCE/POWER, and PRESS TO PUNCH on the Power knob. Preserve ALL functional HUD text, current control selections, meters and any comic combat-event overlays such as KRAK!, COUNTER, WHAM! and SUPER ACTIVE; these are gameplay feedback, not background signage. Preserve the current illustrative state, widescreen aspect ratio and opaque background. Do not add new objects or embellishments.
promptHistory:
Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: illustrated widescreen concept frame for an ORIGINAL browser-based solo 3D boxing game, not a poster or cover. Render a complete 16:9 gameplay viewport with convincing game-camera framing, sophisticated art direction, carefully typeset readable UI, and charming sculpted 3D toy fighters. This is a design concept, not a claim of implemented gameplay.
Fixed user brief: continuous boxing with three rotary controls: Attack (Jab/Cross/Hook/Uppercut), Stance (Defensive/Offensive/Neutral/Super), Power (four levels); press the Power knob to punch. Semi-LEGO-like ORIGINAL human toy boxers with chunky articulated bevelled limbs, oversized padded gloves, expressive original faces, distinct silhouettes, visible toy joints, molded-plastic highlights and printed face details. Do not reproduce a LEGO minifigure exactly or any Marvel characters/logos. Marvel-comic-inspired hand-lettered impact words and graphic energy are desired.
Scene: underground comic fight club in a compact warehouse basement, a real small boxing ring with three ropes per side and modest close-packed stylized toy spectators, worn painted posters, theatrical overhead spotlights. Provisional player is a short broad-shouldered human toy boxer with cobalt gloves and charcoal trunks; provisional rival is a taller lean human toy boxer with red-orange gloves and warm cream trunks. Their specific identities are design placeholders. Both appear athletic, adult, appealing and not realistic humans. No gore.
Composition: one dominant continuous 3D ring viewport, taking around 82% of the screen, behind and slightly above the player's shoulder with player low-left foreground, rival upper-right midground; both glove silhouettes and foot positions readable. No split-screen, no large overlapping fighter portrait, no generic website navigation or cards. A quiet health/name/round strip occupies the top; a compact continuous three-control instrument rail occupies the bottom. Show minimal legible top text "YOU", "ROUND 01", "RIVAL"; distinct health strips. In the bottom rail, show exactly three circular four-detent tactile rotary dials with their currently selected label and a clearly legible section label "ATTACK", "STANCE", "POWER". Four power ticks 1 2 3 4. The Power control has the action text "PRESS TO PUNCH". A compact readable stamina gauge and earned Super gauge support the game without obstructing combat. All required content is visible within a single viewport. The player is the focal subject, not the UI. Make the control rail coherent and restrained, with no bento-card scaffold.
Grounding: ink-black, warm cream/paper, cobalt, red-orange and impact yellow. Large dramatic comic lettering belongs to the contact event or temporary state, never smothering faces, attack tells or meters. Fight should feel cinematic and physically impactful but simple enough for a browser game's reusable primitives and limited materials. Strong contrast, clean legibility, intentional negative space; ornate world details support the fighters rather than distract.

Direction: RINGSIDE FLASH. An underground sports-photographer's decisive contact moment, translated into a 3D toy/comic game. Dark charcoal warehouse envelops the lit ring; a crisp cream spotlight catches shiny cobalt and orange gloves, with the audience falling into restrained shadow. The lighting feels like a ringside flash fired at the instant a punch lands. Angular condensed athletic lettering in the quiet HUD; a single beautiful yellow hand-lettered "KRAK!" burst is placed just behind the point of contact. The player's CROSS has connected; the rival's torso recoils with one foot braced, the toy articulation convincing and punch trajectory readable. Contact is felt through pose and a modest printed impact shape, not a huge explosion. UI selected values are "CROSS", "OFFENSIVE", "3". The top remains small, bottom rail warm cream with black ink markings and physical circular dial textures. One compact "COUNTER" tab can flank the impact. Mood: confident, cinematic, tactile and intense, with unusual editorial restraint. Do not give the player a close-up character portrait outside the fight. Avoid blockbuster photorealism, haze that hides silhouettes, neon sci-fi cyberpunk, excessive chrome, giant gradients, explosions or floating decorative icons.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image is the edit target: illustrated boxing game concept. Change ONLY the bottom control rail. Remove the separate fourth circular punch button to the right of the POWER rotary dial. There must be exactly THREE circular controls in total: ATTACK, STANCE, POWER. The existing POWER rotary knob itself is pressed to punch, so place the exact text "PRESS TO PUNCH" immediately beneath that existing POWER dial. Keep the POWER heading and its four numbered settings readable; arrange that section neatly with enough space. Absorb the removed button's space naturally into the rail; no replacement fourth control. Preserve the entire 3D boxing scene, fighters, poses, facial expressions, camera, lighting, crowd, comic impact words, health bars, stamina and Super meters, chosen values and colour palette. Preserve all UI outside this narrow correction. This is a concept frame; output opaque, same widescreen composition.
